Problems

1. Missing import – The function uses os but never imports it.  
2. Un-handled KeyError – If the variable is not set the code raises a KeyError that the caller may not expect.  
3. Information disclosure – Returning arbitrary environment variables without any filtering can leak secrets (e.g. AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) if the key is supplied from un-trusted input (typical in web APIs or CLI tools).  
4. No documentation or typing – Hard to understand or use safely.  
5. No default/required semantics – Callers often need “give me a default” or “fail fast if missing”.  
6. Case sensitivity portability – Windows names are case-insensitive, POSIX are not; users may want a helper that normalises this.  
7. Mutability exposure – Returning the original string allows later code to mutate os.environ via os.environ[key] = … which may be unwanted; better to return a copy.  

How to fix / improve

```python
# stdlib
import os
from typing import Optional


class EnvError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when a required environment variable is missing."""


def get_env(
    key: str,
    default: Optional[str] = None,
    *,
    required: bool = False,
    _allowed: frozenset[str] | None = None,
) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Safely fetch an environment variable.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : str
        Name of the variable.
    default : str | None, optional
        Value returned when the variable is missing.
    required : bool, keyword-only
        If True, raise EnvError instead of returning default when missing.
    _allowed : set[str] | None
        Optional white-list of keys that may be read; everything else raises EnvError.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        Environment variable value or *default*.

    Raises
    ------
    EnvError
        When variable is required but not present.
    """
    # optional key white-list
    if _allowed is not None and key not in _allowed:
        raise EnvError(f"Access to env var '{key}' is not allowed")

    try:
        value = os.environ[key]
    except KeyError:
        if required:
            raise EnvError(f"Required env var '{key}' not set")
        return default

    # never leak secrets into logs; caller sees full value
    return value[:]  # return a copy to discourage mutation
```

What changed and why

• Added the missing import.  
• Handles absent variables with a default or a clear custom exception; avoids KeyError bubbling unexpectedly.  
• Optional required=True flag lets you fail fast on critical settings.  
• Optional whitelist protects against leaking arbitrary secrets when the key originates from user input.  
• Returns a copy (`value[:]`) so a caller that mutates the string (very rare, but possible with bytearray in Python ≤3.9) cannot modify os.environ by accident.  
• Supplied docstring, typing and custom exception for maintainability.  
• The call site can mask/obfuscate sensitive values when logging (`******`) instead of printing them directly.  
• Cross-platform note: callers can normalise key case (`key.upper()`) if they want case-insensitive behaviour on Windows.  

Security best practices

• Never echo the raw value to logs. Mask with first/last 3 chars or length only.  
• Restrict what can be read if keys come from outside the code base.  
• Consider using a secrets management service (AWS Secrets Manager, Hashicorp Vault, etc.) instead of environment variables for highly sensitive data.
